$comment: CAPTURED FROM A REAL `npx playwright test --reporter=json` RUN — a full 361-case local sweep
on 2026-08-08. Only the bulky per-result payloads (stdout, errors, attachments, durations)
were dropped; every structural fact the gate depends on is exactly as Playwright emitted it:
· config.rootDir is the ABSOLUTE testDir, and spec.file is relative to IT;
· the top-level suite of each file has title === file, and must be skipped or
the filename appears twice in the id;
· a passing case reports test.status "expected" / result.status "passed", a failing one
"unexpected" / "failed", and a skipped one "skipped".
B266086: the first cut of collectCases() was written against a fixture somebody invented and
got the first two wrong, so every id it produced missed the ledger. A fixture you invented can
only confirm what you already believed. This one is real.
RE-CAPTURED 2026-08-08 BY B267537, and the reason is a defect in how the ORIGINAL was pinned.
It held two pond-outlet-clear rows, and the end-to-end test asserts every FAILING id here is
present on the LIVE e2e/known-red.json. B267536 fixed those two cases and removed them from the
ledger — so the guard went red for the ledger SHRINKING, which is the one thing the ledger
exists to be able to do. A guard that fails when its subject succeeds creates pressure to leave
a fixed case listed, which is exactly the amnesty the ledger is designed to prevent.
This capture deliberately carries PASSING cases as well as a failing one (the original had only
failures and a skip), so the status mapping is exercised in every direction. Its one failure,
flood-district-scoping.spec.js:133, is on the local-lane ledger. When THAT is fixed, re-capture
from a real run rather than editing this file by hand — test/e2eDriftGate.test.js says so in its
failure message.
